recipes.review_notes:
Yield converted 2026-08-26 (round 2): yield_amount/yield_unit now hold the real batch weight directly (~19.98kg, rounded to 20kg) instead of a back-derived servings figure. Per the site's updated convention (see HANDOFF_TO_RASPBERRY.md and resep-10's own note) -- checked against real cookbook practice, a sauce/paste yield is always given in volume or weight ('makes about 2 cups'), never 'servings,' since how much sauce counts as one serving is inherently variable. That was the actual root cause of this field needing correcting in the first place. The 550-servings/~222-orders figure below is kept as background context only (useful if anyone wants a rough 'feeds how many' sense) -- it is no longer the literal yield_amount.

Original 2026-08-26 note (superseded as the literal yield_amount, kept for the derivation): Yield estimated 2026-08-26 -- this recipe has no stated batch size (no order/portion count anywhere in the scan), so built bottom-up from total ingredient volume/weight, the same method used for resep-10, then converted to orders using the 90g-sauce-per-order / 2-3-people-per-order convention established on resep-10 and resep-116 that same day.

Ingredient conversion (batch total, terasi excluded -- see caveat below):
- Bawang besar (onion) x25, no unit given: guessed ~250g/onion -> ~6.25kg / ~6.58L
- Cabe merah (canned) x5 cans: reused the #10-can net-drained-weight figure from the red-pepper package-size research (~62oz/can net) -> ~8.79kg / ~8.79L -- unconfirmed this is actually the same canned product
- Dried sliced garlic, 1 bowl: no standard 'bowl' size exists anywhere in the data; guessed ~750mL at a light dried-garlic bulk density -> ~300g
- Sambal pedas, 1/2 container: no standard 'container' size; guessed a ~1qt (946mL) container -> ~520g / ~473mL for the half
- Brown sugar x5 boxes: 16oz/box per package-sizes reference -> 2268g / ~2.76L
- Gula pasir 5 cups, Garam 1¾ cups, Kecap manis 1 cup, Cabe kering 1/2 cup: standard cup (236.6mL) x typical ingredient density -> ~1006g/~1183mL, ~497g/~414mL, ~308g/~237mL, ~41g/~118mL respectively
- Terasi x3 pieces: EXCLUDED from the total. The package-sizes reference's ~4g/sachet figure (for individually-wrapped seasoning terasi) would add only ~12g total, implausibly small next to ~8.79kg of chili in the same pot -- this is almost certainly a terasi block/cake, not a retail sachet, and no real size is known. Flagged rather than guessed.

Total (excl. terasi): ~19.98kg / ~21.3L -- roughly 3x resep-10's batch, consistent with this being a bulk-fried chili/onion base rather than a thin glaze.

Orders/servings: ~19,978g / 90g-per-order ~= 222 orders; at the 2-3-people-per-order convention (2.5 avg) -> ~555 servings, rounded to 550. Range depending on people/order: ~444-666.

Confidence: LOW. Multiple inputs are guesses with no anchor in the data (onion piece weight, 'bowl', 'container', the reused canned-chili size) and terasi is excluded entirely. The 90g/order figure itself was derived for resep-10's fry-then-toss glaze, not confirmed for this dish's likely braised/simmered style, which may use more sauce per order than a tossed glaze -- Arman's call to apply it here anyway as a placeholder ('we can adjust the yield once we know better'). No linked home-scale recipe exists yet for this dish (unlike resep-2/4/8/45's resep-113/114/115/117 pattern) -- revisit this yield_amount once one is created or any of the above package sizes get confirmed.

Sauce-per-order weight established 2026-08-26, separately from the ingredient-volume math above: Arman + Gemini cross-check using BBQ-wings serving norms (6-8 wings ~30-45g sauce), scaled to this dish's 12-13-piece order -> 60-90g; settled on 90g since this sauce is also eaten with rice, not just clinging to the chicken. Same conversation corrected the real-world serving count for one order from 4 down to 2-3 people (see resep-116's review_notes) -- pieces/order didn't change, just how many people split it. This 90g figure describes what's served/eaten per order; it's ~1.5x lower than the ~140g/order this recipe's own ingredient list produces (~7.01kg total / 50 orders), which is expected -- kitchens typically make more glaze than ends up on the plate (tossing-bowl residue, buffer). Both numbers can be true at once: ~140g/order produced, ~90g/order served. yield_amount is intentionally left at 200 (= 50 orders x REF_LINK_SERVINGS's 4, not true servings-per-order) so the site's recipe_ref auto-link still hands resep-116 exactly one order's worth of sauce -- if REF_LINK_SERVINGS ever stops being hardcoded at 4, this number needs revisiting alongside it. Picked volume (L) as the recorded unit since this is a pourable glaze/sauce -- cookbooks state a sauce's yield in cups/liters, not kg, when it's a liquid. The 200-servings figure and the REF_LINK_SERVINGS-alignment rationale above are kept for the historical record but no longer apply: resep-116's 'View recipe' link on this sauce now lands on resep-10 showing its own full recorded yield (6.7L) rather than pre-scaled to one order, matching how a cookbook links from a dish to its sauce's own page.

recipes.review_notes: Split 2026-08-27 into two home-scale dishes -- resep-124 (Ikan Acar) and resep-125 (Pepes) -- since this recipe is really one shared spice paste (bumbu) used for two different final preparations (fried/pickled vs. banana-leaf-wrapped/steamed). No linked_recipe_id set here since the field only holds one id; see resep-124/resep-125 for both. The batch never states how many fish it was designed for -- no fish count, weight, or paste yield anywhere on the source page. Per Arman's direction (2026-08-27), used the same method as resep-11 (Ayam Solo): back-solve a fish count from total spice-paste weight against an external reference (a standard Ikan Acar/Pepes ratio for one ~400-500g whole fish), then divide every ingredient in THIS recipe by that same count, preserving Ramayani's own proportions rather than substituting the reference's ratios. Total spice-paste weight here (chili 1200g + candlenut 1000g + shallot 1000g + garlic 100g + ginger 200g + salt 400g + MSG ~24g + sugar ~113g) is ~4037g. The reference's per-fish spice-paste total, estimated using typical piece weights (shallot ~12g/clove, garlic ~4g/clove, candlenut ~4.5g/piece, chili ~12g/piece), is ~141g/fish. 4037 / 141 = ~28.6, rounded to a batch of **28 fish**. Cross-check: the recipe's tomato (2000g, listed separately from the spice paste, matching the reference's own "aromatic layering" category rather than "spice paste") divides to 2000/28 = 71g/fish -- lining up closely with the reference's own "1/2 medium tomato" estimate, independent support for 28 being a reasonable batch size. Note: dividing each spice-paste ingredient individually by the reference's own per-fish amount gives a much wider spread (implied counts from ~10 to ~67 across ingredients) than the clean, consistent divide Ayam Solo's water gave -- this means Ramayani's actual paste is proportionally heavier on candlenut/salt/sugar and lighter on garlic than a generic reference recipe. That is expected and intentional, not an error -- per Arman's direction, the home version keeps Ramayani's own ratios (computed from the ORIGINAL batch numbers directly, not re-derived from the reference), only using the reference to size the batch overall. The "4 oz" sugar amount is ambiguous -- the adjacent salt line's name_id ("ons Garam") confirms Indonesian "ons" (100g) was mistranscribed into the schema's "oz" unit field for at least that one row; sugar may have the same issue (400g) rather than literal 4oz (113g). Used the literal 113g reading since it isn't explicitly flagged the way salt was, but this is unconfirmed -- if it should be 400g instead, sugar in both home recipes would need revisiting.

recipes.headnote_en: Melt-in your mouth pork belly slices slow steamed in a deeply savory, aromatic soy sauce glaze and served with preserved mustard greens

method.step_en: From Google: Boil & Deep-Fry: Pork belly slabs are parboiled, the skin is pricked and rubbed with rice wine or vinegar, then deep-fried until blistered to create air pockets in the rind.
Slice & Layer: The pork is sliced into uniform slabs and arranged skin-side-down in a steaming bowl over a bed of seasoned preserved mustard greens (sayur asin / meicai) or shiitake mushrooms.
Steaming: The spice-and-soy liquid is poured over, and the entire bowl is steamed low-and-slow for 1.5 to 3 hours. It is inverted onto a serving platter right before dining.

recipes.review_notes: Added 2026-08-27: the source scan never states a pork belly weight -- no amount for the dish's namesake protein anywhere on the page, only the braising liquid. Per Arman's direction, back-solved it the same way as resep-11/resep-14: summed the batch's liquid ingredients (Kikoman 600ml + water 900ml + kecap ikan 225ml + kecap manis 225ml + arak 300ml = 2250ml total, sugar excluded as a dissolved solid, not liquid), then divided by the midpoint of an external reference ratio (450-650 mL liquid per 1kg/2.2lb pork belly, midpoint 550 mL/kg) -- 2250 / 550 = ~4.09 kg, i.e. **9 lbs**, added above as the "Perut babi" line. This is an inference from liquid volume, not a number written on the scan.

The layering order (RED-WHITE-WHITE-GREEN-WHITE-WHITE-GREEN-WHITE-WHITE-RED) matches resep-85's own method step exactly. One correction made here: the Talam Obi top-layer coconut milk was written as "half can (~200ml)" using an outdated can-size assumption -- corrected to 133ml (4 cans x 300ml/can [confirmed via resep-12, see raspberry_package_sizes] / 9). METHOD REVISED 2026-08-24: the first draft's method (8 steps) invented specific technique -- whisking order, "strain", cook times, layer thickness in mm, an unflagged claim that the GREEN colour comes from pandan (pandan isn't in the ingredient list at all) -- none of which is in resep-45/85's actual text (2 sparse sentences total for Kue Pepe, 1 for the layering order). recipes.review_notes:
New recipe added 2026-08-26: home-scale version of resep-5 (Ayam Bumbu Rujak Sauce), calculated from that recipe's own real batch total (~19.98kg / ~21.3L, see resep-5's review_notes) rather than transcribed from a scan. Target yield: about 4 cups (~946ml) -- a ~1/22.5 scale-down factor applied uniformly to every ingredient, then rounded to practical home measures (1 whole onion instead of 1.11, a standard ~14oz can instead of 0.22 of a #10 can, etc.) rather than left as exact fractions. Cooking times shortened from the restaurant method's stages (30/20/15 min) to reflect the much smaller volume -- one sliced onion doesn't need 30 minutes to soften the way 25 onions would.

Two items resolved by judgment rather than by scaling an unknown: (1) terasi -- resep-5's '3 pieces' has no confirmed real size (flagged in its own review_notes), so this uses 1 tsp (~5g), a normal home-recipe terasi quantity, independent of the scale-down factor; (2) oil -- resep-5's method mentions frying in '1 inch' of oil but never lists oil as a formal ingredient row, so there was nothing to scale down for it; 3 tbsp added here as a reasonable pan-frying amount for this size batch. Neither is a confirmed number -- flag for Hertha/Arman if either turns out to matter.

method.step_en: Blend or grind the onion, candlenuts, garlic, ginger, and lemongrass into a smooth paste (food processor or mortar and pestle).

recipes.review_notes:
New recipe added 2026-08-27, revised same day (see below): home-scale version of resep-1 (Bumbu Ayam Kare), calculated from that recipe's own real batch total (~33.63kg, summed from the ingredient list -- onion/candlenut/garlic/ginger/lemongrass by weight, oil/turmeric/MSG/salt/sugar/kencur by volume at typical densities) rather than transcribed from a scan.

METHODOLOGY, locked in 2026-08-27 (Arman): yield_amount/yield_unit is the exact, objective physical quantity a sauce/paste produces -- never adjusted to make anything come out even. yield_per_serving is a subjective conversion factor (how much of that yield one real person eats), and it MUST be derived from the dish that actually uses the sauce/paste, never invented by looking at the sauce/paste alone. Deriving it takes two facts from the dish: (a) the dish's own stated amount of the sauce/paste per dish-portion -- resep-113 says 1 tbsp (dropping the old 'heaping' qualifier, an unmeasurable descriptor) of paste per its own 3-4-piece chicken portion; (b) how many real people that same dish-portion feeds -- resep-113's serves was corrected 2026-08-27 from '1' (a guess made before this framework existed) to '1-2' (see resep-113's own review_notes). yield_per_serving = (a) / (b) = 1 tbsp (3 tsp) / 1.5 (midpoint) = 2 tsp per real serving -- NOT the raw 18g/1tbsp dish-portion figure used in the first pass below, which conflated 'per dish-portion' with 'per real person' exactly the same way the sauces' first-pass yield_per_serving did.

When the dish's own base unit is too small to be a sensible standalone batch (1 tbsp alone isn't worth making), scale up by taking that whole base unit -- paste amount, dish-portions, and people-fed together -- and multiplying all of it by the same integer K. First attempt used K=24 dish-portions specifically to land on whole aromatics units (4 garlic cloves, 9 candlenuts) -- rejected 2026-08-27 as unrealistic (implies feeding ~36 people from one batch, and Arman doesn't remake the same dish often enough to want that much paste on hand). Revised to K=4 (Arman: 'I would imagine somebody making paste for maybe 4-6 orders if they really like it, I rarely make the same dish twice a year') -- within the 4-6 range but toward the lower end matching realistic single-household reuse. At K=4: paste yield = 4 tbsp (12 tsp), feeds ~6 people (4 x 1.5).

Aromatics precision, explicitly relaxed 2026-08-27 (Arman): fractional units like half a garlic clove or one and a half candlenuts are fine -- don't force whole-unit rounding just to avoid a fraction. This let K=4 (rather than a larger K forcing whole cloves/nuts) be the final batch size.

All gram measurements removed 2026-08-27 -- previously mixed precise-looking grams (18g, 432g, 260g) with imprecise volume estimates (~1.5 cups) in the same recipe, which is inconsistent for a home cook measuring by spoon, not scale. Every ingredient and the yield itself are now stated only in tsp/Tbsp/cups.

Unit consistency fix 2026-08-27 (second pass, same day): yield_amount/yield_unit was first set to 12 / 'tsp' specifically so yield_per_serving would divide out to a clean whole number (2) instead of a fraction. Wrong tradeoff -- Arman caught it: resep-113's own ingredient line says '1 tbsp' of this paste, so a reader clicking through and landing on a page denominated in 'tsp' is a jarring, needless mismatch, even though 12 tsp and 4 Tbsp are the same physical amount. Corrected to yield_amount: 4, yield_unit: 'tbsp' (matching resep-113's unit exactly), yield_per_serving: 0.667 (~2/3 tbsp = 2 tsp, same real per-serving amount as before, just expressed in the matching unit) -- accepting a decimal in a field a reader never sees directly (only the computed '~N servings' text is shown) rather than a clean-looking backend number that breaks unit consistency for the reader.

Same assumption as before, still flagged: turmeric and kencur treated as fresh/ground (density ~1.0 g/ml, matching this recipe's other fresh aromatics) rather than dry powder, a judgment call not a confirmed fact -- doesn't change the tsp amounts stated here either way, since those were derived from volume (cups) in the original batch, not from a weight assumption.

Method: stir-fry time shortened further (to 4-5 minutes) for the now much smaller K=4 volume. Storage note (keeps refrigerated/frozen) is standard food-handling knowledge, not an invented specific technique.

resep-113's paste ingredient (recipe_ref) repointed from resep-1 to this recipe -- see resep-113's own review_notes; its amount/unit there was also simplified from '1 heaping tbsp' to plain '1 tbsp' (dropping 'heaping', an unmeasurable qualifier, same fix applied everywhere else in this recipe). Now that this recipe's yield_unit is also 'tbsp' (see unit consistency fix above), the two units match exactly -- no remaining caveat for a future recipe_ref link pre-scaling fix (HANDOFF_TO_RAMAYANI.md) to worry about on this particular pair.

Minimum-quantity floor fix 2026-08-27 (third pass, same day): the site's scaling stepper rounds every tsp-based ingredient to the nearest 1/4 tsp. Viewing this recipe at its smallest meaningful setting -- '1 Tbsp' (exactly 1 dish-portion, matching resep-113's own ingredient line) -- divides every amount by 4. Ginger, turmeric, and MSG were each 1/4 tsp in the full 4-Tbsp batch, so at 1 Tbsp they became 1/16 tsp (~0.06) -- far below the 1/4 tsp rounding floor, so they silently disappeared (rounded to 0) from the ingredient list. Kencur (1/2 tsp) sat exactly on the rounding boundary (1/8 tsp at 1-portion scale), an unreliable edge case either way. Important: this is NOT a batch-size (K) problem -- any K would hit the same wall, since dividing by 4 to reach 1 dish-portion always reproduces the same fixed per-portion ratio, regardless of how big the stored full batch is.

Fix: raised ginger, turmeric, MSG, and kencur from 1/4-1/2 tsp to 1 tsp each in the full batch -- the smallest amount that still divides cleanly to exactly 1/4 tsp (not zero) at the 1-Tbsp/1-portion view. This is a real increase beyond the mathematically 'precise' scaled ratio (4x for three of these, 2x for kencur), not just a rounding nicety -- flagging plainly since it will make the paste noticeably more forward on ginger/turmeric/kencur than a pure scale-down implies. Salt (3/4 tsp), sugar (3/4 tsp), and oil (1 1/2 tsp) were already safely above the floor (divide to 3/16 tsp, which still rounds up to a nonzero 1/4 tsp) and were left unchanged. yield_amount/yield_unit/yield_per_serving unchanged -- this fix only touches individual ingredient amounts, not the overall yield math.

Same floor problem, missed on the first pass, found by checking the live site 2026-08-27 (fourth pass, same day): only checked tsp-based (volume) ingredients against the site's ¼-tsp rounding -- missed that garlic (½ clove) and candlenuts (1½), both counted rather than measured by volume, have no rounding-floor protection at all on the site (no recognized unit lookup for 'clove' or a blank unit, so they just scale by raw decimal with no bucketing). At the 1-Tbsp/1-portion view they became 0.125 clove and 0.375 candlenuts -- both unusable amounts, confirmed live on the deployed site (showed as '0.1 clove Garlic' and '0.4 Candlenuts'). Raised both to a full-batch amount that lands on a clean ½ at 1-portion: garlic ½ clove -> 2 cloves (portion = ½ clove, matching the previously-established 'half a clove is fine' allowance), candlenuts 1½ -> 2 (portion = ½ nut, same allowance). Checked the resulting 1-portion view live on the deployed site for every ingredient after this fix -- nothing rounds to zero or an unmeasurable fraction anymore.

Separate issue found during this same live check, NOT fixed here (site-code issue, not a data issue): at any scaling factor other than 1x, the site displays computed amounts as raw decimals (e.g. '0.3 tsp', '0.5 clove') instead of converting them back to a kitchen fraction the way the *unscaled* page does (e.g. '¼ tsp', '½ clove' at the full 4-Tbsp view). Confirmed by comparing the same recipe's full-batch view (shows nice fractions) against its qty=1 view (shows decimals) side by side. This is a general site-wide formatting gap, not specific to this recipe -- would affect any recipe's stepper whenever scaled away from 1x. Flagged for a possible follow-up spec to ramayani; not something fixable from the data side.

Real internal-consistency error found and fixed 2026-08-27 (fifth pass, same day): Arman pointed out that summing this recipe's own ingredients clearly totals more than the stated '1 Tbsp' at the 1-portion view. Checked by computing the TRUE, scale-invariant per-single-dish-portion amount for every ingredient directly from the original 33.63kg restaurant batch (independent of whatever K is chosen) and comparing to what was stored:
- Onion: true ratio is ~1.84 tsp/portion; stored (¼ cup full-batch / 4) was 3 tsp/portion -- a genuine 63% over-round, not shrinkage. '¼ cup' was picked as a 'clean' full-batch number during an earlier pass without checking it against the actual proportional ratio. Corrected to 2½ Tbsp full-batch (true ratio, ~1.8 tsp/portion) -- switched from 'cup' to 'Tbsp' as the stated unit too, since ¼ cup is an awkwardly large unit for a quantity this small.
- Salt/sugar: true ratio is ~0.15 tsp/portion, below the ¼ tsp floor -- the stored ¾ tsp full-batch (0.1875 tsp/portion) was only surviving display because the site's rounding happened to round 0.1875 up to 0.25, not because the stored number was actually at a deliberate floor. Bumped both to 1 tsp full-batch (matching the same explicit ¼ tsp/portion floor already applied to ginger/turmeric/MSG/kencur) so it's correct by construction, not by lucky rounding.
- Oil: true ratio ~0.32 tsp/portion (already above the floor, no floor needed) -- stored 1½ tsp full-batch (0.375/portion) was close but not exact; tightened to 1¼ tsp (0.3125/portion) to match the real ratio.
- Ginger, turmeric, MSG, kencur, garlic, candlenuts: checked against the same true-ratio math -- all already correct from the earlier floor-fix passes, left unchanged.

After this fix, the full 4-Tbsp batch's ingredients sum to ~90mL, vs. the stated 59mL (4 Tbsp) finished-paste target -- raw ingredients are now ~53% more than the finished paste by volume (a ~34% reduction from stir-frying/blending down), which is a normal, explainable amount of cooking shrinkage for a paste like this, not a data error. Before this fix the gap was much larger (~150%+) and was NOT explainable by shrinkage alone -- that was the actual bug. yield_amount/yield_unit/yield_per_serving unchanged; this fix only corrects individual ingredient amounts to be internally consistent with the recipe's own stated yield.

Natural-unit relabeling 2026-08-27 (sixth pass, same day): Arman's real point, separate from the math fix above -- expressing bulky, discrete ingredients like onion in measured spoons ('2½ Tbsp chopped onion') doesn't read like something a person actually preps; nobody measures chopped onion by the tablespoon. Relabeled onion from '2½ Tbsp' to '¼ small onion, chopped' -- same real quantity (no math change, no change to yield_amount/servings), just phrased the way someone would actually cut it. Garlic (cloves) and candlenuts (count) were already natural units, left as-is. Liquid/powder items (oil, turmeric, MSG, salt, sugar, kencur) keep tsp/tbsp, the natural unit for those. Batch size (¼ onion, ~4 orders/~6 servings) confirmed as-is rather than sized up -- Arman's call, given the option to size up to ⅓-½ onion (~9-12 servings) was raised and declined.

Known follow-on, not addressed here (Arman flagged as a separate, related issue to tackle next): viewing this recipe at its smallest stepper setting ('1 Tbsp' = 1 dish-portion) is itself an unrealistic thing to actually prepare -- and now that onion is stated as a fraction-of-a-whole ('¼ onion') rather than a spoon measure, the site's stepper further subdividing that down to '1 portion' (¼ of ¼ onion) produces an even less meaningful fraction than the tsp-based ingredients do. This is the reason to reconsider whether the stepper should even allow scaling this recipe down to a single dish-portion, separate from the ingredient-math fixes above.

Standing minimum-batch-size rule adopted 2026-08-27 (seventh pass, same day): Arman's fix for the '4 Tbsp is still too small a thing to bother making' problem -- rather than keep deriving batch size from serving-count reasoning (K x people-per-portion), adopt a fixed floor instead: **4 oz / 8 Tbsp / 1/2 cup is the smallest jar size we will ever make of anything.** This is now the minimum yield_amount for any batch-to-home sauce/paste/marinade conversion going forward, applied directly rather than re-derived from servings math each time -- see docs/yield-scaling.md for the updated playbook. Doubled every ingredient from the 4-Tbsp batch to hit this floor (4 Tbsp -> 8 Tbsp): onion 1/4 -> 1/2 small onion, candlenuts 2 -> 4, garlic 2 -> 4 cloves, ginger/turmeric/MSG/salt/sugar/kencur 1 -> 2 tsp each, oil 1 1/4 -> 2 1/2 tsp, lemongrass '1 inch' -> '2 inches'. Doubling is exact and safe here specifically because per-dish-portion amounts (full-batch / K) are scale-invariant under uniform doubling of both the batch and K together -- verified: every previously-floored ingredient (ginger/turmeric/MSG/salt/sugar/kencur at ¼ tsp/portion, garlic/candlenuts at ½/portion) lands on exactly the same per-portion floor at the new K=8 as it did at K=4. Bonus: doubling happens to turn every previously-fractional count (½ clove, ½ onion at the full-batch level) into a clean whole number (4 cloves, ½ onion is now just 'half the onion' rather than 'a quarter'), removing the fractional-aromatics awkwardness entirely rather than just tolerating it.

yield_amount: 4 -> 8 (tbsp, unit unchanged). yield_per_serving unchanged (0.667, still 2 tsp per real person -- this doesn't change just because the batch got bigger). Computed servings: 8 / 0.667 = 12 (was 6), matching the doubled batch feeding double the people. Headnote updated to state the 4oz/half-cup framing explicitly, so it doesn't read as an arbitrary number.

recipes.headnote_en: Ramayani's Babi Hong, scaled down to 1 kg (2.2 lbs) of pork belly from the restaurant's own recipe.

ingredients.name_en: Pork belly, skin on, sliced into slabs

method.step_en: Boil & Deep-Fry: Parboil the pork belly slab, prick and rub the skin with rice wine or vinegar, then deep-fry until blistered to create air pockets in the rind.
